title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin.
lines: Long ago there was a town by a river.
It was a pretty town with pointy roofs.
But Hamelin had a big problem.
They ate the bread and the cheese.
They even slept in people's hats.
The people didn't know what to do.
The mayor was fat and he loved money.
He didn't know what to do.
One day a strange man came to the town.
He had a long coat in every colour.
I can chase the rats away, he said.
But I want a thousand gold coins.
Yes, yes, as long as you chase the rats away.
The man put the pipe to his lips.
He played a strange and beautiful tune.
Rats came out of every house.
Big rats, small rats, grey and brown rats.
The piper walked to the river.
And they swam away, far away.
The piper went to the mayor.
Now I want my thousand coins.
Whoever breaks a promise will be sorry.
He put the pipe to his lips again.
Now he played a different tune.
All the children of the town came outside.
A gateway to a wonderful land.
He gave it to the piper.
I should have kept my promise.
The piper played one more time.
And all the children came dancing back.
From that day on the mayor always kept his promises.
And in Hamelin they still say: A promise is a promise.
